title: Why a sale is designed to make you spend more
description:
A discount does not save you money. It moves the number you are comparing against.

New video every day.

scenes.say: A thing you were not going to buy is now thirty percent off. And suddenly you are buying it.
Nothing about the thing changed. Only the number next to it did.
The old price was never really the price. It was there to be crossed out. Its job is to be the thing the new price looks good against.
Your brain does not judge a price on its own. It judges it against whatever number it saw last. Show it a big number first, and the second one feels like a win.
So you did not save thirty percent. You spent one hundred percent of a number you had not planned to spend at all.
A discount on something you do not need is not a saving. It is a purchase with a compliment attached.
